findings.claim: The Packed-unwrapping rule ("a column's effective kind is col.kind.primitive when kind is a Packed, else col.kind itself") is duplicated verbatim in column_subset and should_encode instead of living in one place. The two call sites will silently drift out of sync if Packed's unwrap rule ever changes (e.g. a second wrapper type, or Packed gaining more than one primitive).
findings.source: columnstore.py:53 `alias = col.kind.primitive if isinstance(col.kind, Packed) else col.kind` and columnstore.py:63 `kind = col.kind.primitive if isinstance(col.kind, Packed) else col.kind`
findings.remedy: Extract a small shared helper, e.g. `_primitive_kind(col: Column) -> str`, and have both column_subset and should_encode call it. No behavior changes for any caller of either function.

findings.claim: `Handle.span` used to be documented as a plain, presumably read-write `span: str` attribute (per the class docstring: "span is a read-only, string-typed view kept for callers written against the old plain-string attribute"), but the new implementation is a property with a getter only -- no setter. Any existing caller that assigns `handle.span = ...` directly (rather than only reading it) would now raise AttributeError instead of working as before. test_lifespan.py only exercises read paths (equality, dict-key, str formatting) -- none of it assigns to `.span` -- so this narrowing from writable attribute to read-only property is not exercised by the provided test suite. The CHANGES.md note itself hedges only for callers that "only ever read .span", implicitly leaving open whether a write-caller exists elsewhere in the package.
findings.source: lifespan.py:70-72 `@property\n    def span(self) -> str:\n        return self._span.value` (no setter); compare lifespan.py:64 docstring "span is a read-only, string-typed view kept for callers written against the old plain-string attribute" and CHANGES.md:2-3 "Handle used to carry a plain `span: str` attribute... It now carries `_span: Span`... with a read-only `span` property"
findings.remedy: Either add a `@span.setter` that accepts a `Span` or a string (coercing via `span_from_value`) so the public attribute stays read-write and behavior-preserving, or, if no caller in the package ever writes `.span`, verify that claim (grep/executable check) and state it plainly in the compat note instead of hedging only on readers.

findings.claim: `QuietQueue` is an unused, unreferenced actor. It is never constructed, never passed anywhere, and nothing in Workspace's init, child(at:), or main.swift's test touches it. It adds a concurrency-isolation type to the file's public surface that does nothing and could mislead a reader into thinking Workspace already has some execution-context story wired in.
findings.source: workspace.swift:57-59 `// Reserved for a future default execution context; not wired into any\n// scoping path yet.\nactor QuietQueue {}`
findings.remedy: Delete `QuietQueue` and its comment. Nothing depends on it (deletion test passes trivially); reintroduce it when an actual caller needs a default execution context, not speculatively.

findings.claim: CHANGES.md asserts "No test's skip/run outcome changes on any platform" for this refactor (combining three per-platform-pair guards into a single is_driftplane guard), but test_platform_guards.py's main() only ever calls collect_skips against MAINLAND and asserts that dict is empty. It never calls collect_skips(GEARSHIFT, ALL_TESTS) or collect_skips(TIDELINE, ALL_TESTS) to check that the three now-combined tests (test_shared_temp_writable, test_process_fork, test_large_page_alloc) still skip on both of those platforms with the expected reason, or that the untouched guards still behave as before. The behavior-preservation claim for gearshift and tideline is reasoning-only; it is invisible to the one platform config (mainland) this suite actually executes.
findings.source: test_platform_guards.py:74-79 `def main() -> int:\n    skipped = collect_skips(MAINLAND, ALL_TESTS)\n    assert skipped == {}, ...` (no equivalent call/assert for GEARSHIFT or TIDELINE); CHANGES.md:11 "No test's skip/run outcome changes on any platform."
findings.remedy: Extend main() (or add cases) to call collect_skips(GEARSHIFT, ALL_TESTS) and collect_skips(TIDELINE, ALL_TESTS) and assert the expected skip set and reason text for each, so the cross-platform preservation claim is backed by executable evidence instead of only a mainland run.
